clue.text: Shaky creature given a form of restraint

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, a creature
a shackle is a fetter, one form of restraint

explanation.surface: An unsteady animal is being fitted with a restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tumbledown and rickety is unsteady, liable to collapse.

clue.text: Drink up when crossing by Hero's place

indicators.note: crossing means one piece straddles, here placed round the other
in a down clue up means the word for a drink is read from bottom to top

parts.note: soda is a drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drinks up while passing by the home of Hero from Greek legend.
explanation.walkthrough: In the legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly from this town to visit Hero, so it is tied to her story; 'up' suits a down clue, giving ADOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient town on the Hellespont is the setting of the Hero and Leander legend.

clue.text: Like a Shropshire lad following a girl to work

indicators.note: following says the boy's name comes after the girl's name and the work

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name
OP is short for opus, a work
Ian is a boy's name, a lad

explanation.surface: A Shropshire lad, as in Housman's poems, trails after a girl on her way to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Like a Shropshire lad' as one phrase, after Housman's poems; 'lad' is really a boy's name and 'to' a link. Salop is an old name for Shropshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop is the old name for the county, so its adjective describes things belonging to that county.

clue.text: Shorten a couple of notes about article in Italian

parts.note: two notes: B on the scale, and the breve

indicators.note: about means the note's letters are wrapped round what follows

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note, the second of the couple

indicators.note: in says the article sits inside the word for Italian

parts.note: IT is short for Italian vermouth
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut a passage of music around an article written in Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of notes' supplies two notes, one a scale letter and one a long note value; the middle reads IAT once the article is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a word or text is to cut it down, making it briefer.

clue.text: Some of the meekest relatives of a high-flyer

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few of a successful person's most timid kin.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'of a high-flyer' as the definition, which cannot stand for a noun; 'of' is a link and 'a high-flyer' the definition. 'the' is also a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This small falcon hovers high over fields, a bird that flies high.

clue.text: Stake raised for a Sicilian mount

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word for a stake is read upwards

parts.note: the ante is the stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: A post is lifted up to serve as a mountain in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: The volcano on the east of Sicily is the island's great mountain.

clue.text: Power supplier unusually keen to conceal a bloomer

indicators.note: to conceal means the shuffled letters hide the flower inside them
unusually says the letters of keen appear in an odd order

parts.note: a rose is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: An energy provider is oddly eager to cover up a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' makes KENE; 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin oil is burnt as a fuel in lamps and heaters, supplying energy.

clue.text: Summary of new cuts introduced as a gamble

indicators.note: introduced means the phrase for a gamble is put into the shuffled letters
new says the letters of cuts are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: done on spec is done speculatively, as a gamble

explanation.surface: A précis of fresh spending cuts brought in speculatively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes CTUS from CUTS, and ON SPEC is 'introduced' into it. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A general survey or synopsis of a subject gives an overview of it.

clue.text: A sword also was the main item in this

indicators.note: in says the word for was the main item sits inside the word for also

parts.note: too means also
led means was at the head, was the main item

explanation.surface: A sword was the chief exhibit in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points back to the answer: the Spanish city is famous for its steel blades, so a sword is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades of fine tempered steel from the Spanish city are called by its name.

clue.text: Returned payment with friend's course outline

indicators.note: Returned means the whole run of letters for payment and friend's is read backwards

parts.note: a sub is an advance payment of wages
an ally is a friend; the 's is added

explanation.surface: A refunded fee goes along with a friend's description of a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns SUB plus ALLY'S as one run, giving SYLLABUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The programme of topics for a course of study is set out in an outline.

clue.text: Vehicles carrying soldiers through large areas?

indicators.note: carrying means the word for large areas holds the soldiers inside

parts.note: tracts are large expanses of land
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Lorries transporting troops across wide stretches of country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm machines that pull ploughs are motor vehicles.

clue.text: Wine? How about it?

parts.note: as can mean how, in the way that

indicators.note: about means the word it is turned round

parts.note: taken as written, then turned

explanation.surface: Someone offers wine and asks if their guest fancies some.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a casual offer of a drink; 'How about it?' is really two pieces, with 'about' as the turning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Piedmont town gives its name to a sparkling white Italian wine.

clue.text: A ship initially seaworthy but open to attack

indicators.note: initially says only the first letter of the word ship is used

parts.note: sailable means fit to be sailed, seaworthy

explanation.surface: A vessel looks fine for sea at first but proves vulnerable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' goes with 'ship' only; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be assailed is vulnerable, liable to be assaulted.

clue.text: Country people seem agitated after native upheaval

indicators.note: after says the second shuffled word comes later in the answer
upheaval says the letters of native are thrown into disorder
agitated says the letters of seem are stirred up

explanation.surface: Locals seem disturbed following an uprising among the indigenous population.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams, each with its own signal: 'upheaval' gives VIETNA and 'agitated' gives MESE.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of the South-East Asian nation are its people.

clue.text: Head-banger who took on the Mouse King

definitions.text: who took on the Mouse King

explanation.surface: A headbanging rocker who fought a royal rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: In Tchaikovsky's ballet, based on Hoffmann's tale, the wooden toy comes to life and battles the Mouse King.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool that splits shells bangs nut, slang for head; and the toy hero of the Christmas ballet fights the Mouse King.

clue.text: Backward youths outside are able to cause general indignation

indicators.note: outside means the turned word for youths goes round the other piece
Backward means the word for youths is read in reverse

parts.note: lads are youths
can means are able

explanation.surface: Retrograde young men abroad are capable of causing outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns LADS into SDAL, which goes 'outside' CAN. 'to cause' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Public outrage over a disgraceful act is one dictionary sense of the word.

clue.text: Be involved in a right harangue, behaving abnormally!.

indicators.note: involved in means the word Be is taken inside the rest

parts.note: a rant is a harangue
taken as written

explanation.surface: Take part in a proper tirade, acting strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark is part of the surface; the stray full stop after it is a print artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviating from the normal course, the word describes conduct that departs from the usual.

clue.text: One learns to be extremely decisive in a daring feat

indicators.note: in says the picked letters go inside the word for a daring feat

parts.note: a stunt is a daring feat

indicators.note: extremely means only the first and last letters of decisive are used

explanation.surface: A pupil must be firm in carrying out a bold exploit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link; 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for decisive but picks its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil or scholar is someone engaged in learning.

clue.text: Fish disappeared inside? Bother!

indicators.note: inside means the word for disappeared sits within the exclamation

parts.note: drat is a mild curse, like bother
gone means disappeared

explanation.surface: A fish has gone missing indoors: how annoying!
explanation.definitionFit: A small spiny marine fish of the genus Callionymus goes by this name.

clue.text: Captain taking exercise on the spot

explanation.surface: A ship's master works out without going anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: one who jumps a rope in place is doing just that.
explanation.definitionFit: The master of a boat or team leader is in charge; and one who jumps rope exercises in one place.

clue.text: It keeps channels open and encourages conversation

explanation.surface: Something that keeps waterways clear and gets people talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channels' suggests television or communication, but it means frozen sea lanes.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong-hulled ship clears frozen sea lanes; a party game or remark eases strangers into talk.

clue.text: An afterthought outside 17's range

indicators.note: outside means the afterthought goes round the learner's letter

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
17 across is a learner, and L is the learner's plate letter

explanation.surface: A late addition beyond a pupil's scope.
explanation.walkthrough: '17' points to the across answer, a learner, abbreviated to L as on a learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The great European mountain chain is a range.

clue.text: A river, swallows up a holiday quickly

indicators.note: swallows up means the river's name takes the other word inside it

parts.note: the Po is a river in northern Italy
a rest is a break, a holiday

explanation.surface: A river engulfs a vacation fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction means at a rapid tempo, fast.

clue.text: First-class journey over the Rockies, starting and finishing here

definitions.text: First-class journey over the Rockies, starting and finishing here

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

indicators.note: starting and finishing means only the first and last letters of Rockies are taken

parts.note: a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A luxury flight across the Rocky Mountains that takes off and lands at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting and finishing' gives RS from Rockies; the whole clue also describes a landing strip where such a flight begins and ends. 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of ground where aircraft take off and land is where flights begin and end.

clue.text: Understand Head departed to get file

indicators.note: Head departed means the first letter of the word for understand goes

parts.note: to grasp is to understand

explanation.surface: A headmaster has left so the file can be obtained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse metal tool for smoothing wood is a kind of file.

clue.text: Dog exercises in front of family quarters

indicators.note: in front of says the exercises come first

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises
kin means family
E, S, E are points of the compass, quarters

explanation.surface: A dog works out ahead of the family's living space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings, but it means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Chinese breed with long hair is a type of dog.

clue.text: Bands seen around river vessels

indicators.note: seen around means the word for bands is set round the river letter

parts.note: lines are bands or stripes

explanation.surface: Musical groups spotted beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' suggests musicians, but it means stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: Large passenger ships on a regular route are vessels.

clue.text: Fellow escapes from boring summing-up

indicators.note: escapes from means the letter for fellow leaves the word for boring

parts.note: perforation is the act of boring a hole

explanation.surface: A man flees from a tedious recap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like tedious, but it means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing part of a speech recapitulates its main points.
